title: The constant-rank groupoid norm polynomial and its evaluation
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with maps $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$, and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] satisfying the groupoid laws [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. Write $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$, and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. Assume $A\ne0$ and that both $s,t$ are finite locally free of the same constant degree $r\ge1$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For $a\in A$, let $\sigma[T],\tau[T]:A[T]\to B[T]$ be the coefficientwise polynomial extensions fixing $T$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and set
$$
P_a(T)=N_{\sigma[T]}(T-\tau(a))\in A[T].
$$
Here $N_{\sigma[T]}$ is the finite locally free norm [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts]: on each local free chart it is the determinant of multiplication by the input element, and these determinants are glued. The norm polynomial has the form
$$
P_a(T)=T^r+\sum_{j<r}p_jT^j,\qquad
\sigma(p_j)=\tau(p_j)\quad(j<r).
$$
In particular $P_a\in C[T]$ is monic of degree $r$. Its construction also satisfies
$$
P_a=N_{\sigma[T]}(\tau[T](T-a)),\qquad
\bigl(\sigma[T](P_a)\bigr)(\tau(a))=0.
$$
With $p_r=1$, its evaluation comparison is
$$
\tau(P_a(a))=\sum_{j=0}^r\tau(p_j)\tau(a)^j
=\sum_{j=0}^r\sigma(p_j)\tau(a)^j
=\bigl(\sigma[T](P_a)\bigr)(\tau(a))=0.
$$
The identity map induces $\epsilon=e^\sharp:B\to A$ with $\epsilon\circ\tau=\operatorname{id}_A$ and
$$
P_a(a)=\epsilon(\tau(P_a(a)))=0.
$$
No global free basis of $B$ over $A$, reducedness, or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-norm-characteristic-polynomial] to σ, r and τ(a). The defining unique-existence assertion identifies the polynomial norm selected for σ[T] with the polynomial norm in the theorem: each satisfies IsLocallyFreeDeterminantNorm and uniqueness equates them. This gives monicity, degree r and evaluation at τ(a) equal to zero. Monic.as_sum gives the expansion using the actual coefficients P.coeff j; the coefficient in degree r is one. Coefficientwise polynomial extension fixes X, so the specified norm of X-C(τ(a)) is also the norm of τ[T](X-C(a)).

proof.text: Use full faithfulness of Spec to identify σ and τ with the ring maps extracted from their spectrum morphisms. Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-canonical-norm-charts] directly to the extracted coefficientwise source map and the extracted target image of X-C(a). Uniqueness and the preceding identification show that its canonical norm value is P. This supplies precisely the affine-open section norm chart formula, with the same dependent scalar structures, required by the polynomial invariance theorem.

source.place: Tags 02DU(1), 02DV(1),(3), and 03BJ, second paragraph: identify the local determinant norm with the scheme norm used by Tag 03BH.

proof.text: Construct the groupoid on points directly from [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]: objects are maps H→U and arrows x→y are maps a:H→R with a≫s=x and a≫t=y. Identity, inverse and composition are induced by e, i and pullback.lift followed by c. Endpoint, unit, inverse and associativity axioms give the Groupoid structure; the arrow equivalences are identities. Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-polynomial-norm-invariant] to F=X-C(a), P, this point groupoid and the chart formula from the preceding step. It gives σ[T](P)=τ[T](P). Comparing coefficients gives σ(P.coeff j)=τ(P.coeff j) for every j, hence in particular j<r. The coefficient criterion for Polynomial.lifts puts P in the polynomial ring over the equalizer subring.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), second paragraph, application of Tag 03BH (groupoids-lemma-determinant-trick) to the polynomial groupoid

proof.text: Put $p_r=1$. Applying the ring homomorphism $\tau$ to the finite sum defining $P_a(a)$, then replacing each $\tau(p_j)$ by $\sigma(p_j)$ using step 3, gives $\tau(P_a(a))=\sum_{j=0}^r\tau(p_j)\tau(a)^j=\sum_{j=0}^r\sigma(p_j)\tau(a)^j=(\sigma[T](P_a))(\tau(a))=0$, where the last equality is step 1. These are just preservation of sums, products and powers by a ring map and the definition of polynomial evaluation.

source.place: Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), second paragraph: invariant coefficients imply target pullback of the evaluation is zero

proof.text: The identity law $t\circ e=\operatorname{id}_U$ in [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws] gives $\epsilon\circ\tau=\operatorname{id}_A$ for $\epsilon=e^\sharp$. Apply $\epsilon$ to the equality of step 4: $P_a(a)=\epsilon(\tau(P_a(a)))=\epsilon(0)=0$. This uses the specified identity section, and hence does not require a separate faithful-flatness assertion.
